strategy.summary: Groupby float sum overflow in the Cython group_sum kernel (pandas._libs.groupby) returns NaN instead of inf because Kahan compensation becomes NaN when the running sum or input is infinite; the fix (PR 63132) resets non-finite compensation to 0 for float32/float64 and complex types. Reproduce by running the added parametrized test test_cython_group_sum_overflow in pandas/tests/groupby/test_libgroupby.py on the buggy commit a7e0900cfb75 (expected to fail) and on the fixed revision (expected to pass). Build pandas from source as a Cython extension since the kernel is compiled code.

pinned_because: numpy==1.26.4 pinned from issue#60303 (undocumented, era-inferred from the report; not a README constraint), chosen to match the reporter's environment
pytest==8.3.3 pinned from issue#60303 (undocumented, not numerically relevant)
hypothesis==6.72.4 pinned from issue#60303 (undocumented, not numerically relevant)
python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython left unpinned: documented in README without a version constraint, so latest compatible versions are used

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/groupby/test_libgroupby.py::test_cython_group_sum_overflow (parametrized over 8 value cases: float64 max/min, several complex128 combinations, and complex(3.0 + min*1j) and complex(max + 3j))
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision a7e0900cfb75: the float64 cases (np.finfo(np.float64).max and .min summed three times in one group) return NaN where inf/-inf is expected, and the complex cases return NaN components, so tm.assert_numpy_array_equal fails for those parametrizations. On the fixed revision (PR 63132): all 8 parametrizations pass, group_sum returns inf/-inf and complex(inf, ...) values as expected.
risks: Overflow behaviour depends on compiled Cython code; the test must run against a build of the buggy and fixed commits, so a stale editable build would give false results.
Reproduction through the public API (Series.groupby.sum, resample) may not match the direct group_sum call used in the test; the test path is the authoritative one.
Test comment indicates the old numpy version needed a separate test fix; numpy 1.26.4 is inferred from the issue, not documented, so behaviour under other numpy versions is unverified.

The fix is tied to Kahan compensation; the maintainer noted it is unclear whether overflow can be handled consistently while staying performant, so the fixed revision's behaviour for non-test inputs may differ.

Platform-specific floating-point behaviour (e.g. x87 extended precision, ARM vs x86) was not stated in the evidence; the strategy assumes standard IEEE-754 float64 on a typical x86_64 Linux platform, which is not confirmed.
Python version is not stated in the evidence (null), so it is left to the environment default compatible with numpy 1.26.4.

oracle.reference_source: pandas/tests/groupby/test_libgroupby.py test expected values (inf, -inf, complex(inf, ...)) compared via tm.assert_numpy_array_equal
oracle.why: Overflow to infinity is an exact IEEE result expected by the test; the comparison is exact rather than tolerance-based

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy revision the group_sum kernel accumulates compensation that becomes NaN once an infinite value enters the Kahan term, so the result array holds NaN where the test expects inf; tm.assert_numpy_array_equal sees NaN != inf and the assertion fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the compensation is reset to 0 when non-finite (real part checked for complex), so the sum yields inf/-inf as expected and tm.assert_numpy_array_equal succeeds for all 8 parametrizations.
